fields.why: Doubling times (days, with CIs) are a headline result and are a continuous quantity; A filed them under count/rate, which is meant for rates per population or person-time. The brief does not say how a model-derived parameter such as a doubling time or growth rate is typed.

'Multinomial regression' of lineage shares is a multinomial logit, the natural generalization of logistic, but the family table lists no multinomial entry; both readers gave the other value as alternative_reading. A rule 'multinomial (logit) regression → logistic' would settle it.

Converting the model's growth rate to a doubling time (ln2/r) is arithmetic on a model coefficient, like VE = 100 × (1 − OR), which the brief lists as not a procedure; it is not a transformation of the data.

The report's stated aim is to summarize 'U.S. trends in variant proportions' and its claims are the temporal succession of lineages, which supports trend (A); B's view that this is routine descriptive surveillance is also defensible.
The brief says unadjusted is true 'when the model itself has no covariates'; the multinomial nowcast has time as its only predictor, which B itself notes ('No covariates enter the model').

brief_issues: Family table lacks multinomial regression; outcome_types does not cover model-derived parameters (doubling time, growth rate); 'before/after or trend' needs a line separating trend designs from routine surveillance time series.
